text:
Predicates:
GrowthStock(x) ::: x is a growth stock.
EarnProfits(x) ::: x is bought to earn profits from rapid price appreciation.
SuitableForRetirementFund(x) ::: x is suitable for a retirement fund.
MatureStock(x) ::: x is a mature stock.
KO ::: KO stock.
Volatile(x) ::: x's price is volatile.
Premises:
∀x (GrowthStock(x) → EarnProfits(x)) ::: All growth stocks are bought to earn profits from rapid price appreciation.
∀x (EarnProfits(x) → ¬SuitableForRetirementFund(x)) ::: If a stock is bought to earn profits from rapid price appreciation, then it is not suitable for a retirement fund.
∃x GrowthStock(x) ::: Some stocks are growth stocks.
∀x (MatureStock(x) → SuitableForRetirementFund(x)) ::: All mature stocks are suitable for a retirement fund.
MatureStock(KO) ::: KO is a mature stock.
Conclusion:
(GrowthStock(KO) ∨ EarnProfits(KO)) → (¬Stock(KO) ∧ ¬Volatile(KO)) ::: If KO is a growth stock or bought to earn profits from rapid price appreciation, then KO is neither a stock nor is its price volatile.
